protocol_addenda.timing: before either marked-birth table was opened locally or any count was scored
changes: add a nested birth-mark-controlled age slope as a diagnostic only
freeze the N^-5/6 collision-ratio adversary without fitting an exponent
state explicitly that a slope rejects only coarse-state lumpability and may proxy unrecorded current geometry

primary_estimator.stratum: canonical primitive projective line (ell_u,ell_v) within size and orientation
primary_estimator.aggregation: sum over site/mark fields; direct rows and null lines cannot enter the rank-one risk set
primary_estimator.interpretation: linear-probability next-step hazard change per unit occupied-density age after line fixed effects; beta=0 is no continuous K1 dependence

collision_estimator.role: separate direct 0->2 diagonal mass; estimated jointly with beta rather than used as a tail-law fit

nested_mark_diagnostic.estimator: the same one-degree age slope with fixed-effect strata refined from ell to (ell,mark01_axis,mark01_diagonal,mark01_landed,mark01_h4)
nested_mark_diagnostic.allowed_fields: only strict 0->1 birth marks already known at K1; no K2/mark12 outcome-side field enters the control
nested_mark_diagnostic.purpose: measure whether the primary slope attenuates after controlling recorded birth-local geometry
nested_mark_diagnostic.boundary: survival after this control still may reflect unrecorded current configuration geometry at k0 and is not intrinsic temporal memory

six_arm_collision_adversary.Dbar: equal orientation mean (D_first+D_second)/2 within each size
six_arm_collision_adversary.score: one-degree covariance-aware contrast Dbar_425-fixed_ratio*Dbar_325 using the full within-size batch covariance and block-diagonal cross-size covariance
six_arm_collision_adversary.geometry_caveat: the two size designs are not a matched fixed-shape lineage, so failure may be amplitude/shape drift rather than failure of the conditional six-arm exponent
six_arm_collision_adversary.interpretation: failure is not evidence against or for thermal Q4

complement_check.score: apply the identical line-stratified age estimator to (K1c,K2c,k0c)
exact_gates: all six stored complement-audit failure sums are zero for each archive
direct-birth mass is invariant under the transform
complement_check.boundary: forward and complement slopes are paired views of one archive, not independent evidence and not assumed equal

covariance.delete_one_unit: one common batch index removed simultaneously from first and second orientations within a size
covariance.cross_orientation: retained within each size because the two orientations share counter-keyed permutations
covariance.cross_size: zero only because the N325 and N425 seeds and replica domains are disjoint

inference.orientation_test: two-sided Student t test of beta_age=0 with 99 degrees of freedom
inference.size_joint_test: two-degree covariance-aware Wald test of first_beta_age=second_beta_age=0, reported once per archive
inference.collision_interval: two-sided 99 percent Student-t interval; no asymptotic D_N law is fitted

claim_boundary: This is a retrospective reanalysis of two revealed P267 archives and creates no independent evidence rows.
A resolved birth-age slope rejects lumpability of the recorded coarse state (k,rank,ell); it may proxy unrecorded current geometry and is not by itself intrinsic temporal memory.
The nested birth-mark diagnostic controls recorded geometry at K1 only; it does not observe the full current configuration at k0.
D_N is a separate collision channel and is not used to explain or subtract the age slope.
No exact 1/57 witness, finite D_N census or six-arm exponent calculation is repeated.
The two orientations of one size remain one covariance block.
